parents.subject: Less Commonly Taught Languages
parents.course: Elementary Course in a Less Commonly Taught Language II

ns2:section.sectionText: This three-quarter sequence focuses on the acquisition of basic speaking, listening, reading and writing skills in modern formal and spoken Armenian. The course utilizes the most advanced computer technology and audio-visual aids enabling students to master the alphabet, a core vocabulary, and some basic grammatical structures in order to communicate their basic survivor's needs in Armenian, understand simple texts and to achieve a minimal level of proficiency in modern formal and spoken Armenian. A considerable amount of historical-political and social-cultural issues about Armenia are skillfully built into the course for students who have intention to conduct research in Armenian Studies or related fields, to visit or to pursue work in Armenia. A language competency exam is offered at the end of spring quarter for those taking this course as college language requirement. Winter and Spring quarters. This section is offered through the BTAA Course Share Program hosted by University of Chicago and will be video-conference/Zoom/online taught for participating universities.
